$comment: tag: flock = Flock's own claim; independent = documented by others; both = claimed and corroborated; unknown = nobody outside Flock has verified it.

hops.title: Photons hit the sensor
hops.summary: The passive infrared sensor fires on any warm moving object. The camera takes six to twelve stills of the vehicle's rear, lit at night by the 850 nm ring.
unknowns: People and cyclists are in frame when they trigger it; Flock says they are not indexed

hops.title: Edge inference on the Snapdragon
hops.summary: The on-board model reads the plate and its state with a confidence score and describes the vehicle: the 'Vehicle Fingerprint'. Video never leaves the camera; crops and text do.

hops.title: Time and place are stamped
hops.summary: Timestamp, GPS position from the patch antenna and the device identifier are attached.
unknowns: Direction of travel as an indexed field is not confirmed in any public source

hops.title: Uplink over LTE
hops.transport: HTTPS, TLS 1.2 or higher, over a carrier SIM
hops.summary: A few kilobytes per read leave over the cellular module. In January 2026 dozens of devices were found answering on public carrier addresses with an unauthenticated admin page, which is how much of the software stack became public.

hops.title: Ingest and encrypt
hops.summary: Flock's architecture document describes validation on arrival and encryption with AWS Key Management Service.

hops.title: Process and index
hops.summary: Microservices make the read searchable and fan alerts out through Amazon SNS. Redshift and QuickSight handle aggregate analytics. Video products use MP4 and HLS streams; plate readers do not.

hops.title: Store
hops.storage: Images in S3 (AES-256 at rest); structured data in RDS; unstructured in DynamoDB. Criminal-justice (CJIS) data in GovCloud US-East.
hops.summary: Images go to object storage, records to databases. Flock says only CJIS-classified data lives in GovCloud; whether the bulk read lake does is not stated.
unknowns: Whether the bulk plate-read lake is in GovCloud
A FIPS 140 certificate for Flock's modules is asserted but not publicly locatable

hops.title: Hot list match
hops.summary: The plate is compared against NCIC, NCMEC, AMBER, state and custom lists. Lists are pushed to cameras about twice a day, so a plate cleared from a list can keep alerting for up to twelve hours.

hops.title: Alert to an officer
hops.summary: A hit sends plate, image, location and list source to nearby officers' phones within about ten to fifteen seconds. Multi-factor login became mandatory only in August 2026. Audits in Roseville and Los Angeles found 71% and 32% of alerts involved misread plates.

hops.title: Search across the network
hops.summary: Any user in a customer agency can search by plate, description, natural language, or co-travelling vehicles, across their own cameras, their sharing partners, and the national lookup that roughly three quarters of law-enforcement customers joined. In April 2025 one Texas deputy's query reached 83,345 cameras in 6,809 networks.
unknowns: Whether derived metadata is deleted on the same clock as images

hops.title: Audit row
hops.summary: Each search writes a row. FOIA'd exports show the fields. Other agencies' searches of your cameras appear with the operator and plate redacted. EFF found about one in five reasons across 12 million searches were vague; ALPRWatch found rows changing after the fact.

hops.title: Delete
hops.retention: 7 days by default since 13 August 2026; 30 days before that; longer where an elected body approved it; Evidence Mode preserves specific data indefinitely
hops.summary: An S3 lifecycle policy removes images at the configured interval and logs the deletion to CloudTrail. Flock's own pages still disagree on whether the default is 30 or 7 days.

retentionPresets.label: 30 days
retentionPresets.note: Flock default until Aug 2026; Oregon cap; still shown on some Flock pages

retentionPresets.label: 60 days
retentionPresets.note: California Highway Patrol cap under SB 34

retentionPresets.label: Evidence Mode
retentionPresets.note: Cold storage for an active investigation; no published limit

deputy.reasonAsLogged: had an abortion, search for female
deputy.note: Reproduced from the audit log of a Johnson County, Texas search reported by 404 Media and documented by EFF. No warrant. The reach shown is the number the log recorded.
